items.headline: Bubble or Fatigue? The Stock Market Needs to Decide—Now
items.summary: Stock markets have been firmly set in a “beat and raise” focus heading into the start of a crucial earnings season, and their reaction Tuesday to a manifestly impressive set of figures from the world’s biggest chip maker suggests anything less than perfection likely will disappoint.  Samsung impressive second-quarter earnings, which included a near 20-fold increase in profit and a doubling in overall revenue, failed to add any extra juice to a market already foaming with speculative fever for all things tech following a red hot first half of the year.  The question for investors, heading into both the second-quarter earnings season and the traditional lull of the summer months, is whether the market’s initial reaction to the stellar, but not door-busting, numbers from the chip maker are a sign of tech stock fatigue or a coded bubble warning for the world’s hottest trade.
